question.problem: If the speed of an object is measured in $\text{feet/min},$ what are the units of its acceleration?
question.worked_solution:
We can find the acceleration of an object by computing the slope of its speed-time graph. So, let's draw an example of a speed-time graph where the speed is measured in $\text{feet/min}$ and the time is measured in $\text{min}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14265567/assets/2152cd701002de9a804df6fe489fecd7cbd4fd1a3878962b7cad5799c1fd5b3d.png)

In this case, the slope is computed as

$$
m=\frac{\text{change in speed}}{\text{change in time}},
$$

and so the units of the slope are as follows:

$$
\frac{\text{units of speed}}{\text{units of time}}=\frac{\text{feet/min}}{\text{min}}=\frac{\text{feet}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{1}{\text{min}}=\frac{\text{feet}}{{\text{min}}^{2}}
$$

Therefore, the units of acceleration are $\frac{\text{feet}}{{\text{min}}^{2}}.$
